prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production game sprite atlas for H.E.X. Confluence, matching the attached original pixel-art environmental props. Create a transparent-background 4-column by 4-row atlas with exactly sixteen separate props, each fully inside its own equal square cell with generous transparent gutter. Every cell has a grounded bottom baseline, top-left light, crisp deliberate pixel clusters, dark warm brown outlines, olive foliage, brass/gold highlights, same small fantasy pixel-art style and 3/4 overhead viewing angle as the reference. No characters, writing, border, numbers, labels, drop shadow, floor tile, gradients or blur.
Columns left to right are four recognizable original prop families: (1) large round-canopied oak tree with gnarled visible trunk; (2) narrower young leafy tree; (3) fern and reed cluster; (4) low mossy stone ruin wall with three or four large blocks.
Rows top to bottom are four terrain reactions, preserving each prop's identifiable silhouette and dimensions:
Row 1: fire-scorched version, charcoal branches/leaves or blackened stone, tiny glowing ember crevices, visible living silhouette, NOT engulfed in huge flame.
Row 2: frozen version, hoarfrost and discrete blue ice crystals clinging to branches or stones, recognizable plant shapes underneath.
Row 3: flooded version, saturated dark greens, wet lower trunk/stone and a tiny quiet shallow turquoise puddle around the foot, small reeds, no overhead water jets.
Row 4: shadow/blight version, desaturated purple-gray leaves or purple moss, subtle tiny violet growths, darkened ground-facing surfaces, still same recognizable object.
All 16 are complete isolated objects with alpha transparency around them, do not touch or overlap neighboring cells. Maintain consistent scale per column across all four rows. Fixed pixel art, no soft painted detail, no decoration beyond requested prop. This is a usable atlas, exactly 4 by4, high separation and clear shapes.
